elements.element: Customer has the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits termination by “either Party,” and subsection (a) expressly refers to termination by the Company “for convenience pursuant to Section 4.1.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is ninety (90) days, not 30 days.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no obligation to refund prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis or otherwise.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits termination by “either Party” on 90 days' notice and does not expressly restrict HDI's termination right to the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Customer has the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits termination by “either Party,” and subsection (a) expressly recognizes the Company's termination “for convenience pursuant to Section 4.1.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60–90 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires ninety (90) days' written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is limited to the aggregate fees payable under Section 3.1 for the three calendar months preceding the Termination Date.

elements.element: Vendor has a right to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits termination by “either Party,” which includes HDI.

elements.element: Vendor may exercise its termination-for-convenience right only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause does not require HDI's Termination Date to coincide with the end of the initial or a renewal term; the notice may specify a Termination Date without that restriction.

elements.element: Vendor must give 90 days' written notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires either Party to give ninety (90) days' written notice.

result.reason: The redline implements the fallback customer notice period and reduces the termination payment to three months' fees, but it does not restrict HDI's convenience termination right to the end of a term. It therefore fails the fallback as well as the preferred position. Because it does not reach a complete level, it is not minimal as defined. The remaining term and renewal structure is generally preserved without an apparent contradiction.
